Let’s talk about something that can really change your life— Chapter five: Beginning the Process of Change—Awareness and Small Shifts.
Breaking free from lifetraps isn’t about sheer willpower or some quick fix. It’s more like a slow unfolding—a journey that starts with awareness, and grows through those little, consistent changes you make each day. We’re not here to erase the past, but to loosen the grip of those old habits, and give ourselves a bit more room to think, feel, and act in new ways.
So, where do you start? The first step is just to notice your lifetraps as they come up—without judging yourself. It’s about catching those familiar emotions or behaviors in the moment and gently naming what’s happening. Maybe you think to yourself, “Oh, this is my abandonment lifetrap kicking in,” or, “Here I go again with my unrelenting standards.”
When you name the pattern, you put a little space between yourself and that old automatic reaction. Suddenly, it’s not running the show—you are.
Once you’re aware, the next move is to actually question those beliefs that keep the lifetrap alive. Ask yourself things like, “Is this belief really true, or is it just a leftover from my past?” or, “What facts actually support or challenge this thought?” And think, “How would I respond if a good friend was in my shoes?”
These questions help loosen up the grip of old beliefs and open up new possibilities for you. It can be super helpful to jot some of this down in a journal—write about the times your lifetraps get triggered, and experiment with different ways you might respond.
Now, here’s where it gets practical. Try out small behavioral experiments. It might feel awkward or even scary at first, but these little steps make a big difference. Maybe you reach out to someone for support, even though you’re bracing for rejection. Or you set a boundary, even when it feels risky. Maybe you just let yourself mess up, without beating yourself up over it.
None of this is about getting it perfect. It’s about testing the edges of those old beliefs. Every small win, no matter how tiny, builds your confidence and chips away at the power those lifetraps hold over you.
Remember, change doesn’t always happen in a straight line. There’ll be setbacks and doubts along the way. That’s just part of the process. What’s really important is practicing self-compassion—treating yourself with the same patience and kindness you’d show a close friend. And don’t be afraid to lean on others for support, whether it’s friends, support groups, or even a professional.
Over time, these small shifts really add up. The lifetraps start to lose their power, and new, healthier patterns begin to take root. Sure, the journey keeps unfolding, but each step forward brings you a little more freedom, resilience, and self-acceptance.
